items.title: Iran threatens 'decisive' military response to US Hormuz blockade

featured_image.name: Three US aircraft carrier groups and 10 destroyers blockade Strait of Hormuz  | The National

items.description: Iran's top military command threatened the United States on Saturday with a "decisive response" if Washington continues what Tehran calls a blockade of its ports and acts of "armed maritime piracy" in the Strait of Hormuz, escalating a naval standoff that has virtually shut down one of the world's most critical energy corridors.

items.title: Macron calls EU defense clause 'stronger' than NATO's

featured_image.name: Leaders of France and Greece say the EU's defense splurge is no ...

items.description:
French President Emmanuel Macron declared Saturday that the European Union's mutual defense clause is "stronger" than NATO's Article 5, as he used a visit to Athens to reinforce Europe's push toward greater self-reliance amid deepening doubts over the United States' commitment to transatlantic security.

Speaking alongside Greek Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis after talks at Maximos Mansion in Athens, Macron described the EU's Article 42.7 — which obliges all member states to aid any member that comes under armed attack — as "inviolable" and "not up for debate." He warned that "all our potential, or real, enemies need to be very clear about that."[1][2]

items.title: Chernobyl anniversary marked as IAEA warns damaged shield needs repair

featured_image.name: Chernobyl could face 'catastrophic' collapse as repairs stall following  Russian drone strike | Euronews

items.description:
As Ukraine marks the 40th anniversary of the Chernobyl disaster on Sunday, the legacy of a Russian drone strike on the facility's protective shield continues to fuel fears of a new nuclear crisis in the heart of Europe.

On February 14, 2025, an Iranian-designed Shahed 136 drone struck the New Safe Confinement (NSC), the $2.1 billion steel arch built to seal radioactive remnants of Reactor No. 4, tearing a six-meter-wide hole in the structure and igniting fires in its insulation layers. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said the drone carried a "high-explosive warhead" and accused Russia of a deliberate attack. Russia denied the allegations, claiming Ukraine fabricated the incident to disrupt peace negotiations.[1][2][3]

items.title: UK and Finland condemn Israeli killing of journalist in Lebanon as 'intolerable'

featured_image.name: Amal Khalil: Israel Accused of War Crimes After Journalist Death

items.description: The United Kingdom and Finland on Saturday jointly condemned Israeli attacks on journalists in Lebanon, calling the violence "intolerable" in a statement issued in their capacity as co-chairs of the Media Freedom Coalition. The declaration came three days after Lebanese journalist Amal Khalil was killed in an Israeli airstrike on the southern Lebanese village of al-Tiri on April 22.[1][2]

items.title: Traders warn Hormuz oil shock will force harsh demand crash

featured_image.name: Oil rises after Iran, US attack ships as tensions escalate over Hormuz

items.description: The Strait of Hormuz crisis, now approaching its second month, has thrust the United States into the role of emergency supplier to the world while top energy traders warn that the worst of the demand shock is still ahead. With the vital waterway largely closed since late February and diplomatic efforts stalled, global oil markets face a collision between record American exports and an accelerating collapse in consumption.

items.title: Iran rejects 'maximalist' US demands as Pakistan hosts peace push

featured_image.name: Iran says it won't accept 'maximalist demands' as Islamabad hosts peace  push | Reuters

items.description: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi on Saturday laid out Tehran's demands and rejected what it called "maximalist" U.S. positions during talks in Islamabad, as Pakistan pushed to revive diplomacy and end a war that has killed thousands and disrupted global energy markets.[1][2]

items.title: Trump cancels Witkoff-Kushner trip to Pakistan for Iran talks

featured_image.name: Trump to send envoys to Islamabad as Iran rules out direct talks

items.description:
President Donald Trump abruptly canceled a planned trip by envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner to Pakistan for peace talks with Iran on Saturday, Fox News reported, just one day after the White House had confirmed the two would travel to Islamabad for a second round of ceasefire negotiations.[1][2][3]

The cancellation came after Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi left Islamabad on Saturday evening without meeting any American representatives, according to two Pakistani officials who spoke to the Associated Press on condition of anonymity. Araghchi had met with Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and Army Chief Field Marshal Asim Munir during his brief stay, but his government had made clear from the outset that no direct talks with U.S. officials were planned.[4][5][6]

items.title: Palestinians vote in first Gaza election in 20 years

featured_image.name: Gaza area votes in first municipal election in 20 years

items.description:
Palestinians across the occupied West Bank and in the central Gaza city of Deir al-Balah cast ballots on Saturday in municipal elections, marking the first vote in Gaza in two decades and the first electoral event in either territory since the start of the Israel-Hamas war in October 2023.

Polling stations opened at 7 a.m. local time, with nearly 1.5 million people registered to vote in the West Bank and approximately 70,000 eligible in Deir al-Balah, according to the Ramallah-based Central Elections Commission. Polls in the West Bank were set to close at 7 p.m., while those in Deir al-Balah were scheduled to shut at 5 p.m. to allow for counting in daylight, given the lack of electricity in the war-ravaged territory.[1][2][3]

items.title: U.S. envoys head to Pakistan as Iran refuses direct talks

featured_image.name: White House confirms Steve Witkoff, Jared Kushner Pakistan trip for Iran  talks

items.description:
U.S. special envoy Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner are headed to Islamabad on Saturday for what the White House has called a second round of peace talks with Iran, even as Tehran insists it will not engage in direct negotiations with American officials.[1][2][3]

Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi arrived in the Pakistani capital on Friday evening and on Saturday met with Pakistan's army chief, Field Marshal Asim Munir, and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif. But Iran's foreign ministry spokesperson Esmail Baqaei said Araghchi's discussions would be limited to "high-ranking Pakistani officials," with Iran's positions conveyed to the U.S. side through Pakistani mediators.[4][2][5][6][7]

items.title: Traders warn Hormuz oil shock is about to crash global demand

featured_image.name: Why shadow tankers are the only ships still moving through the Strait of  Hormuz

items.description: Nearly two months after the closure of the Strait of Hormuz plunged global energy markets into turmoil, the world's largest oil traders are warning that the worst is yet to come — not from the supply side, but from the demand destruction that is now spreading beyond Asia and into the broader global economy.

items.title: U.S. Navy begins clearing Iranian mines from Strait of Hormuz

featured_image.name: US says it's clearing Iranian mines in effort to open the Strait of Hormuz

items.description: The U.S. Navy is working to clear Iranian mines from the Strait of Hormuz, a vital waterway through which roughly 20% of the world's oil supply typically passes, even as a fragile ceasefire between the United States and Iran shows signs of strain and diplomatic efforts to end the weekslong war remain uncertain.[1][2]

items.title: IEA chief says oil crisis has permanently broken fossil fuel industry

featured_image.name: IEA approves third term for chief Fatih Birol pushing clean energy,  ETEnergyworld

items.description:
The oil crisis triggered by the war in Iran has irreversibly changed the global fossil fuel industry, turning countries away from oil and gas toward cleaner alternatives, International Energy Agency Executive Director Fatih Birol said this week.

"The vase is broken, the damage is done — it will be very difficult to put the pieces back together. This will have permanent consequences for the global energy markets for years to come," Birol told The Guardian in remarks reported on Thursday.[1][2]

items.title: Iran rules out direct talks as U.S. envoys head to Pakistan

featured_image.name: Kushner, Witkoff to Pakistan for Iran talks without Vance - CNBC

items.description: President Donald Trump is dispatching special envoy Steve Witkoff and son-in-law Jared Kushner to Islamabad on Saturday for a second round of negotiations aimed at ending the war between the United States and Iran, though Tehran has already ruled out meeting the Americans face to face.

items.title: EBRD to sign Chernobyl repair deal on 40th anniversary

featured_image.name: Chernobyl Containment Dome Damaged by Russian Drone Strike - MeidasTouch  News

items.description: As the world prepares to mark the 40th anniversary of the Chernobyl disaster on April 26, fresh warnings about the safety of the stricken nuclear plant have thrust the site back into the global spotlight — more than a year after a Russian drone strike punched a hole in its protective shield.

items.title: Chornobyl marks 40th anniversary under threat of war

featured_image.name: Satellite photo shows Russian troops were stationed in Chernobyl's  radioactive zone | WLRN

items.description: As Ukraine prepares to mark the 40th anniversary of the Chornobyl nuclear disaster on Sunday, April 26, the decommissioned plant remains haunted not only by the legacy of the 1986 catastrophe but by the dangers of Russia's ongoing war, which has introduced risks that workers say they never imagined.

items.title: Dutch scientists propose Bering Strait dam to stabilize Atlantic currents

featured_image.name: Study: Erosion has made the Bering Strait a meter deeper on the Alaska side  than it used to be

items.description: A pair of Dutch researchers has put forward one of the more audacious geoengineering concepts in recent memory: building a massive dam across the Bering Strait, the 50-mile channel separating Alaska from Siberia, in an effort to prevent the collapse of the Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation, the system of ocean currents that helps regulate Earth's climate.

items.title: G7 wraps Paris talks with seven deals but no climate discussion

featured_image.name: FRANCE-G7-ENVIRONMENT-POLITICS-DIPLOMACY

items.description: France wrapped up a two-day meeting of G7 environment ministers in Paris on Friday after deliberately excluding climate change from the agenda, a move the French government described as "pragmatic" but critics called a capitulation to the United States under President Donald Trump.

items.title: Trump says Iran preparing offer as US envoys head to Pakistan

featured_image.name: Iran to make offer aimed at satisfying US demands, Trump says | Reuters

items.description:
President Donald Trump said Friday that Iran is preparing a proposal aimed at meeting U.S. demands, as the White House confirmed it is dispatching two senior envoys to Pakistan for a fresh round of diplomacy aimed at ending the war.

"They're making an offer and we'll have to see," Trump told Reuters in a phone interview, adding that he did not yet know the specifics of the proposal. Trump has repeatedly insisted that any deal must require Iran to surrender its enriched uranium and guarantee the free passage of oil through the Strait of Hormuz.[1][2]

items.title: EU and US agree to accelerate steel tariff talks

featured_image.name: Tariffs, Šefčovič in Washington to close deal. EU aims at a 10 per cent  "flat" tariff

items.description:
EU Trade Commissioner Maroš Šefčovič and US Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick have agreed to speed up negotiations over transatlantic steel and aluminum trade, following high-level meetings in Washington this week aimed at breaking a long-standing deadlock over 50% US tariffs on European metals.[1][2]

Šefčovič proposed that both sides return to the concept of "ringfencing" their steel sectors and trading on "very favorable terms," according to statements relayed through financial news wires on Thursday. The meetings, held April 22-24, marked Šefčovič's first visit to Washington since the EU-US trade agreement was concluded in July 2025.[3][4][5][6]

items.title: US sanctions major Chinese refinery, 40 shippers over Iran oil

featured_image.name: Here's How Much Scott Bessent Is Worth

items.description:
The Trump administration on Friday imposed sanctions on Hengli Petrochemical (Dalian) Refinery Co., Ltd., one of China's largest independent oil refineries, along with approximately 40 shipping companies and tankers for their role in transporting Iranian oil, the Treasury Department announced.[1]

The action, carried out under the administration's "Economic Fury" campaign, represents the latest escalation in Washington's effort to sever Iran's primary revenue source — its oil exports — amid the ongoing U.S.-Iran conflict that has disrupted global energy markets since February.
